title: Why AI architect resumes get rejected
oneliner: 'AI enthusiast' gets you binned. Show real work with named frameworks and measured savings, list your published articles, and say what you did single-handedly.
says: Common rejection reasons: writing 'AI enthusiast' or 'AI aspirant' instead of real work; not showing actual implementations with frameworks like RAG or ReAct with savings quantified in percentages or dollars; omitting articles or work published on social media; and not highlighting which key work you did single-handedly within team projects.
explained: Every point targets the same failure: claiming interest instead of demonstrating delivery. 'Enthusiast' is an admission there is no work to describe. A bullet that says 'built a RAG support assistant that cut ticket handling 30%' answers the only question a screener has - can this person produce results? - with a number attached.

The solo-versus-team point is subtle and important. Team achievements are real but ambiguous; reviewers discount what they cannot attribute. Explicitly claiming the parts you drove alone converts group credit into personal evidence. And the published-articles point closes the loop with his sharing advice from reel #14 - public writing is not vanity, it is resume infrastructure.
takeaway: Rewrite every resume bullet as: what I built, with what framework, saving how much - plus what I alone drove, and where my published work lives.
